solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Spinning-wheel in inn mostly used after tea

indicators.note: used after places the shortened inn behind the tea in the answer

parts.note: char is an informal British word for tea

indicators.note: mostly means the word is taken all but its final letter

parts.note: a khan is an Eastern inn or caravanserai

explanation.surface: A spinning-wheel stands in a pub, mostly put to use once tea is over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'inn' looks like the pub of the surface, but here it is the Eastern caravanserai, trimmed by 'mostly'; 'used after' sets it behind the British slang for tea.
explanation.definitionFit: A charkha is the hand-operated spinning-wheel of India, made famous by Gandhi.

clue.text: Flourished with a new tart

parts.note: fl. abbreviates floruit, 'flourished', used of a person's active dates

explanation.surface: Someone finishes a fresh tart with a flourish.
explanation.walkthrough: FL is the abbreviation for floruit, Latin for 'flourished', printed before a historical figure's dates.
explanation.definitionFit: A flan is an open pastry case with a filling, which is a kind of tart.

clue.text: Planet almost has girl

parts.note: Mars is the fourth planet from the sun

indicators.note: almost means the word has is taken short of its last letter

explanation.surface: A planet nearly possesses a girl, like a science-fiction abduction.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' drops the final letter of 'has'; the planet comes first.
explanation.definitionFit: Marsha is a female first name, so it is an example of a girl.

clue.text: Between South America and North America a tan can be made by hot wind

indicators.note: Between asks for something to sit in the gap between the two continents
can be made says the letters of the words a tan are formed into something new

explanation.surface: Somewhere between the two Americas a hot wind can give you a suntan.
explanation.walkthrough: 'can be made' rearranges the letters of 'a tan' into NTAA, which 'Between' places in the gap separating the two continents' abbreviations.
explanation.definitionFit: The Santa Ana is a hot, dry wind that blows from inland deserts over southern California.

clue.text: For oarsman to make error is way to get dinner

definitions.meaning: a rower who fouls a stroke by failing to clear the blade from the water
literally, seizing a crustacean from the sea to eat

explanation.surface: An oarsman's blunder is likened to a method of obtaining a meal.
explanation.walkthrough: The rowing sense is the idiom; the second reading takes the same words at face value, as a fisherman would.
explanation.definitionFit: Rowers use the phrase for a botched stroke that jams the oar; read literally it describes seizing a crustacean for a meal.

clue.text: Road surface in Scotland created by Seth, perhaps

parts.note: in Scottish surnames Mac- means son of, so the Scots form of a son's name opens this way
Seth was the son of the first man in Genesis, so his begetter is named here

explanation.surface: A road surface laid in Scotland is credited to someone called Seth.
explanation.walkthrough: Seth is Adam's son, so in Scotland he would be a MacAdam. The road surface is named after the Scottish engineer John McAdam.
explanation.definitionFit: Macadam is a road-building material of compacted broken stone, often bound with tar.

clue.text: Lie out: shall I wear trousers?

indicators.note: out says the letters of the word lie are taken out of the phrase that follows

parts.note: the letters L, I and E taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone stretched out wonders whether to put on trousers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' removes L, I and E, in that order, from SHALL I WEAR, leaving SHAL-W-AR.
explanation.definitionFit: Shalwar are loose pleated trousers worn in South Asia, often with a long tunic.

clue.text: Father gets squeeze as something for the night

parts.note: pa is an informal word for father
to jam is to squeeze or press tightly

explanation.surface: Dad receives a hug in the form of a bedtime gift.
explanation.walkthrough: 'as' is taken as written, not as a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Pajamas, the American spelling of pyjamas, are loose clothes worn for sleeping at night.

clue.text: Fanfare for girl, brown girl

parts.note: Tara is a female first name
tan is a light brown colour
Tara again, a female first name

explanation.surface: A trumpet flourish is played to honour two girls, one with a tan.
explanation.definitionFit: Taratantara imitates the sound of a trumpet call, so it names a flourish of brass.

clue.text: Eccentric people have Henry behind main rotating rod

parts.note: cranks are odd, obsessive people
H is the symbol for the henry, the unit of inductance
aft means at or towards the back, especially of a ship

explanation.surface: Oddballs have someone called Henry trailing behind them.
explanation.walkthrough: H is the symbol for the henry, a unit of electrical inductance.
explanation.definitionFit: A crankshaft is the principal turning shaft of an engine, driven by the connecting rods.

clue.text: Crop that's cold and uncooked

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for cold, as on taps
raw means not cooked

explanation.surface: A harvest that is chilly and eaten unprepared.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Crop' is not a harvest but a bird's throat pouch.
explanation.definitionFit: A bird's crop is the pouch in its gullet, and craw is another word for that pouch.

clue.text: In this year Mary and Albert are in Jamaica to find screenwriter

indicators.note: are in says the pieces before it sit inside the island's abbreviation

parts.note: HA abbreviates hoc anno, Latin for in this year
BV stands for the Blessed Virgin, Mary
Al is the short form of Albert

explanation.surface: A couple named Mary and Albert holiday in Jamaica this year, hoping to find a film writer.
explanation.walkthrough: Two conventions help: hoc anno is Latin for 'in this year', and the Blessed Virgin stands for Mary. 'are in' places all three inside the island.
explanation.definitionFit: Ruth Prawer Jhabvala wrote the scripts for many Merchant Ivory films, winning two Oscars.

clue.text: Gilbert's work arranged as bald blab

indicators.note: arranged says the letters of the following words are set in a new order

explanation.surface: A Gilbert piece is set out like a bald gossip.
explanation.walkthrough: 'arranged' rearranges the letters of AS BALD BLAB.
explanation.definitionFit: The Bab Ballads are W. S. Gilbert's comic verses, published before his operettas with Sullivan.

clue.text: Incarnation in the Bible's a sailor

parts.note: AV is the Authorised Version, the King James Bible
tar is an old word for a sailor

explanation.surface: The Bible tells of a seafarer as a divine incarnation.
explanation.walkthrough: AV is the Authorised Version of the Bible; 'in' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: In Hinduism an avatar is a deity's descent into bodily form on earth, an incarnation.

clue.text: It's magic for bounder going from one woman's undergarment to another

parts.note: A means one
a bra is a woman's undergarment
a cad is a dishonourable man, a bounder
another undergarment of the same kind, again one bra

explanation.surface: A cad moving from one woman's lingerie to the next works like a spell.
explanation.walkthrough: 'going from' one undergarment 'to another' sets the bounder between two identical pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Abracadabra is the word a conjuror says while performing a trick, so it stands for magic.

clue.text: Jelly covering a fish and mushroom but lacking rice essentially

indicators.note: covering in a down clue puts the first part above the second

parts.note: a gar is a long-snouted fish

indicators.note: lacking says the mushroom word goes without the letters that follow

parts.note: agaric is a type of mushroom

indicators.note: essentially points to the core letters of the word rice

explanation.surface: A jelly is laid over fish and mushrooms but has no rice to it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'essentially' takes the core of 'rice', which 'lacking' removes from the mushroom; 'covering' puts the article and fish on top in this down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Agar-agar is a gelatinous substance from seaweed used to set foods and cultures.

clue.text: Fast time of goat with a level of proficiency

parts.note: ram here means a male goat; also a male sheep
a dan is a grade of skill in judo and karate

explanation.surface: A goat earns a skill grade, as if at a martial arts class.
explanation.walkthrough: A DAN is a grade in martial arts such as judo.
explanation.definitionFit: Ramadan is the Islamic month in which Muslims refrain from eating during daylight hours.

clue.text: Calendar graduate found in turbulent canal

indicators.note: found in says the graduate is placed inside the scrambled letters
turbulent water is churned up, so the letters of canal are stirred about

parts.note: an MA is a Master of Arts, a graduate

explanation.surface: A graduate's calendar is fished out of a choppy canal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turbulent' stirs up the canal's letters, and 'found in' sets the graduate's degree among them, after the first two.
explanation.definitionFit: An almanac is a yearly publication listing dates, tides and astronomical data.

clue.text: Hat for parents in North America? On the contrary

indicators.note: in would put the parents inside the continent
On the contrary flips the container, so the continent goes inside the parents

parts.note: pa and ma are the two parents

explanation.surface: Are hats for parents living in North America? Quite the opposite.
explanation.walkthrough: Read plainly, the parents go inside the continent; 'On the contrary' swaps the roles, so the continent goes inside the parents.
explanation.definitionFit: A panama is a lightweight straw hat originally made in Ecuador.

clue.text: Dance after some go west for old game

indicators.note: after puts the dance behind the turned piece
go west in an across clue means reading from right to left

parts.note: part means some of something
a ball is a formal dance

explanation.surface: Some people head west after a dance, for an old-fashioned game.
explanation.walkthrough: 'go west' reads 'some' backwards in this across entry; 'after' puts the dance behind it.
explanation.definitionFit: Trapball is an old English bat-and-ball game in which a ball is flipped up from a trap.

clue.text: Beside the world tree god creates squared stone

indicators.note: Beside sets the tree next to the god in the answer

parts.note: in Norse myth the world tree Yggdrasil is an ash
a lar is a Roman household god

explanation.surface: Next to the cosmic tree a deity makes a block of dressed stone.
explanation.walkthrough: The Norse world tree Yggdrasil is an ash; LAR is one of the Roman household gods.
explanation.definitionFit: Ashlar is masonry of cut, squared blocks laid in regular courses.

clue.text: Cry 'Ball!'

parts.note: a shout of the word ball sounds like a word for crying loudly

explanation.surface: A shout of 'Ball!', as on a sports field.
explanation.walkthrough: To cry is to weep or shout; the word that means wailing sounds just like 'ball'.
explanation.definitionFit: To bawl is to cry or shout loudly, and it is pronounced like ball.

clue.text: Unruly beggar, maybe mad actor, losing head is embraced by a high-caste Indian

indicators.note: is embraced by says the shortened actor goes inside what follows

parts.note: a Brahman is a member of the highest Hindu caste

indicators.note: losing head means the first letter of the word drops away

parts.note: a ham is an actor who overplays wildly

explanation.surface: A wild beggar, perhaps a crazed actor, gets hugged by a high-caste Indian after losing his head.
explanation.walkthrough: 'losing head' strips the first letter from the overacting performer, and 'is embraced by' tucks what remains inside the Indian, splitting it after its fourth letter.
explanation.definitionFit: An abraham-man was a vagrant of Tudor times who feigned madness to beg.

clue.text: Address to Queen delivered by mother in the morning

parts.note: ma is an informal word for mother
a.m. means in the morning

explanation.surface: Mother delivers a speech to the Queen one morning.
explanation.walkthrough: Royal protocol: the Queen is addressed first as 'Your Majesty', then as 'Ma'am'.
explanation.definitionFit: Ma'am is the polite form used when speaking to the Queen.

clue.text: And was Hamlet at first troubled to tell it from a hawk?

definitions.text: And was Hamlet at first troubled to tell it from a hawk?

indicators.note: at first takes the opening letter of the prince's name
troubled means stirred up, so the letters are mixed

explanation.surface: Was Hamlet really troubled to distinguish a hawk from something else?
explanation.walkthrough: 'at first' takes H from HAMLET; 'troubled' mixes it with AND WAS. Hamlet says he knows 'a hawk from a handsaw' when the wind is southerly.
explanation.definitionFit: Hamlet claims he can tell a hawk from this tool, so the whole clue points to the saw in his line.

clue.text: Procession with one vehicle after another

parts.note: a car is a motor vehicle
A means one
another vehicle, here a van

explanation.surface: A procession forms as one vehicle follows another.
explanation.walkthrough: 'one' sits between two different vehicles, the first a motor car.
explanation.definitionFit: A caravan is a company of travellers moving together in a line, such as a train of camels.
